punchline: Gilbreth did not speed up the bricklayer. He adjusted the scaffold.
thirty_sec: In Taylor's account, Frank Gilbreth used an adjustable scaffold, brick frames and tempered mortar to cut the motions per brick from eighteen to five; in 1914 he and his wife broke with Taylor and founded their own firm.
question: In the task that looks slowest on your team, which unnecessary step around the person could you remove this week instead of pushing the person?
key_contrast: The setup got faster, not the man.
